entries.592dcdcca2b3b49d: The company is an insurance holding company, and as of March 31, 2026, the company, 198 subsidiaries and 255 affiliates make up the group. The flow of money at a life insurance company is in a different order from that of a company that makes and sells products. It first receives premiums from policyholders, sets aside most of them as policy reserves to prepare for future payments, and also invests them in securities, loans and other assets; when events such as death, hospitalization, annuity payment or surrender occur, it pays insurance benefits, annuities, benefit payments and surrender refunds. The 'premium and other income' placed in the revenue column of this table is the portion of these that consists of premiums received from policyholders. Premium and other income for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥6,944,066 million, and in the consolidated statement of income in the securities report, ¥11,308,275 million, obtained by adding investment income of ¥3,735,313 million and other ordinary revenue of ¥628,895 million to this amount, is placed at the top as 'ordinary revenue'. In other words, premium and other income is part of ordinary revenue, and neither of them is a net figure showing size after deductions, as revenue is for a general business company. On the payment side, insurance claims and other payments were ¥6,447,114 million (insurance benefits ¥1,808,520 million, annuities ¥1,037,349 million, benefit payments ¥777,298 million, surrender refunds ¥1,289,905 million, other refunds ¥1,534,039 million), and provision for policy reserves and others, to prepare for future payments, was ¥1,814,937 million.
